Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask.

Summary below and I attached a one-page checklist plus a first-pass BYOK proposal. Key points:

- Operator access model:
  - Default: Redwood operators have zero access to customer CMKs. The customer-provided keystore (KMS/HSM) holds the key material. Redwood retains only encrypted key references and tokenized metadata.
  - Breakglass: there is an auditable, tightly-scoped "breakglass" workflow for emergency decrypts that requires: customer approval (via documented admin contact), two Redwood approvers (SRE + Security), and live recording. We log all steps and emit proof artifacts to the customer's audit S3.

- Subprocessor surface:
  - Runtime GPUs / infra partner: may see encrypted blobs and ephemeral KV caches but never key material.
  - Telemetry aggregator: collects anonymized latency/cost metrics; we can opt-out and route telemetry to customer's collector (recommended).

- Cross-border/data flow:
  - Control plane: metadata routing and model catalog calls are region-aware; customer data (prompts, responses, KV cache) stays in-customer VPC unless explicitly routed.
  - If telemetry is enabled and not routed to customer's collector, aggregated metrics (no plaintext content) may transit US regions per our performance pipelines.

Attachments included: redwood-byok-proposal-v1.pdf, operator-access-matrix.xlsx (matrix has roles/permissions + audit artifacts we will emit).

Next steps:
  1) I will align with Karthik on a short runbook for the breakglass + operator checklist.
  2) Naomi will prepare the DPA addendum draft and pull the SOC2 excerpts we can share.
  3) We can schedule a 30-min sync with Novocare SecOps on Wednesday — does 15:00 ET work?

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T11:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment — key custody and operator access questions

Jasmine — scribbling out the technical sketch here so Novocare SecOps has a concrete view. Please paste this into the shared runbook and link it in the Docusign.

- Key lifecycle:
  - Provision: Customer uploads CMK into their KMS (AWS KMS or on-prem HSM). Redwood stores a key identifier (key_arn) and never persists raw key material.
  - Use: Redwood service endpoints call customer KMS via a dedicated VPC endpoint; requests are signed with a service principal only allowed to CallEncrypt/Decrypt for that key_arn.
  - Rotation: Rotation is customer-triggered. Redwood will honor key_id changes and supports a dual-key acceptance window for rollover.

- Operator roles (minimal):
  - SRE-ops: can view key identifiers, logs, and error traces; cannot call decrypt.
  - Crypto-ops (escalation): can initiate the remote call sequence but the call itself requires customer-side approval token (time-limited).
  - Infra vendor: has host-level access but is prevented from accessing KV cache at rest via kernel-key encryption.

- Telemetry/data egress:
  - By default we will ship only aggregated metrics (latency, token counts). If Novocare prefers, we will turn off external telemetry and route logs/metrics into their collector via a TLS-forwarder inside the VPC.

- Evidence & timing:
  - We can deliver a SOC2 extract (PII handling controls) and an operator access log snapshot for a 30-day window within 3 business days of request.
  - DPA addendum: Naomi is drafting; expect a first cut by EOD Monday.

Please confirm the list of customer admin contacts who will serve as the approval authority for breakglass (we need two contact emails).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

1) DPA addendum: please include the explicit clause that Redwood operators cannot derive key material and the concrete steps for the breakglass approval, including a requirement to deliver a signed incident report within 48 hours.

2) Subprocessors: we need a signed attestation of the vendor list and the last audit date for each subprocess. Can you provide the current subprocessor manifest and point-in-time audit dates?

3) Evidence delivery: SOC2 excerpt is acceptable but we also need a sample operator access log for a 90-day window (redacted) and the TLS-forwarder config if you plan to ship metrics into our collector.

If you can provide the DPA addendum draft and the subprocessor manifest by Tuesday COB (2026-11-16), procurement can move the contract to Legal review. We are amenable to a DocuSign path for the addendum (link preferred).
